question: What's the Right Way to Translate a WordPress Site Into Another Language?
metaDescription: A dedicated multilingual plugin handles content translation properly — a browser auto-translate tool isn't the same and shouldn't be relied on for real use.
shortAnswer: A dedicated multilingual plugin (WPML, Polylang, or a similar established option) is the standard, correct approach — it lets you maintain genuinely separate, properly translated versions of every piece of content, with correct URL structure, hreflang tags for SEO, and a language switcher, rather than relying on a browser's automatic translation, which doesn't create indexable, properly structured translated content at all.

image.alt: A site with genuinely separate, properly translated content versions managed through a dedicated multilingual plugin, not just browser auto-translation
image.prompt: Create a clean, professional technical illustration of one piece of content existing as several properly maintained language versions, connected by a language switcher. Dark navy background, indigo and teal accent colors, flat minimal geometric style, no text, no logos, no people.

bodyHtml:
Why Browser Auto-Translate Isn't a Real Solution

A browser's built-in translation feature (or a simple JavaScript translation widget) translates content on the fly for that one visitor's session, but it doesn't create actual translated pages search engines can index, doesn't let you refine translations that come out awkward or incorrect, and provides no proper URL structure distinguishing language versions — it's a convenience for an individual visitor, not a genuine multilingual site strategy.

What a Proper Multilingual Setup Provides

  • Genuinely separate, indexable content per language, each with its own URL, letting search engines properly rank and serve the right language version to the right audience.
  • Correct hreflang tag implementation, telling search engines which language/region each version targets, which is essential for proper international SEO and avoiding duplicate-content confusion across language versions.
  • A translation management workflow, whether human translators, a professional translation service integration, or careful manual editing of machine-translated drafts, rather than accepting raw automatic translation as the final product.
  • Consistent handling across the whole site, including WooCommerce product data, plugin-generated content, and theme strings, not just the obvious page/post content.

Setting Up Multilingual Content Properly

  1. Choose an established multilingual plugin (WPML, Polylang, or a comparable option) rather than relying on browser-based auto-translation.
  2. Plan a proper translation workflow, using professional translation for important content rather than accepting raw machine translation everywhere.
  3. Confirm hreflang tags are implemented correctly for proper international SEO.
  4. Test the full experience in each language, including any ecommerce or form functionality, not just static content.

Need a multilingual WordPress or WooCommerce site set up properly? See WordPress bug fix.
